assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration-correction of electron lenses opened the door to routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms, interfaces and defects. It is an invention that changed what can be seen across materials physics, chemistry and nanoscience, and the capability is realised in commercial instruments worldwide. From my own field I judge the impact as decisive and the instrumentation as the original experimental realisation.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider led the realisation of the hexapole corrector for the TEM, and Urban led the implementation and demonstration of atomic-resolution imaging with it. These three form a natural and fairly attributable trio. Scherzer's earlier theorem and the contributions of Krivanek and colleagues on STEM correctors are a credit question that the committee must examine carefully.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated in the late 1990s, independently confirmed by many laboratories and now standard in the field for over two decades. Recognition is timely, arguably late.
uncertainties: Whether the STEM-corrector work (Krivanek, Dellby and others) should share credit is not resolved by the supplied credit list.
My own field affinity may bias my weighting, and I treat the scientific record as recalled rather than independently verified here.
Whether the Nobel mandate is judged to cover instrument inventions of this type relative to a physics discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock concept (magic-wavelength trapping) and its realisation gave atomic clocks fractional uncertainties at the 10^-18 level and opened new tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to a redefinition of the second. It is a clear invention with a verified experimental outcome.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock idea and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock; Ye drove the dramatic performance gains and many precision applications. Hall, Hänsch, Wineland and others have already been honoured for related precursor work. The two proposed names are cleanly supported.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) confirm and compare clocks at the 10^-18 level; the physics is stable. The redefinition of the second is pending but the work is mature.
uncertainties: Other contributors, such as Ludlow, Bloom, Takamoto, Hinkley, Ye's group colleagues and Pál Vamos or Kimble-lineage trapped-ion clock researchers, may be argued to be decisive.
Ion clocks (Wineland) were already recognised, so the incremental claim should be judged carefully.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 experimental observation of correlated insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter. The experiment was original, reproducible and led to a very large new field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original 2018 experiments, in which Yuan Cao was the lead author and a graduate student. Credit for the experiment is concentrated in the group leader, but the committee must be sure about the contributions of the graduate student and of other early groups (Dean, Efetov, Young and others).
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by several groups within a few years, with large follow-on activity including fractional Chern insulators. The physical interpretation of superconductivity is still debated, so the maturity is good for the discovery itself but not for all the mechanisms.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled.
Whether the prize should be directed at theory plus experiment, or at the experimental discovery alone.
Role of hBN-encapsulation (Dean, Watanabe, Taniguchi) in sample quality is credited in a separate entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent manipulation of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond created a solid-state platform for room-temperature quantum sensing, nanoscale magnetometry and quantum registers. It is an experimental discovery of a new door onto nanoscale phenomena, with applications in materials, biology and quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated optical detection of single NV spins (1997) and coherent control; Lukin and others led the development of NV-based quantum registers and nanoscale sensing. The 1997 Gruber et al. experiment came from Wrachtrup's group, so the original experimental credit seems best supported with Wrachtrup and Jelezko. Lukin's inclusion rests on later work and on later sensing contributions, which is less clearly the original discovery.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many groups and commercial sensors exist. Applications continue to develop but the underlying discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Credit for the sensing applications is spread widely (Awschalom, Hanson, Yacoby, Walsworth, Hollenberg, Lukin and others).
The relationship between the original single-centre detection and the later sensing impact can be seen as a compound discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in iron pnictides (LaFeAsO1-xFx) opened a second family of high-Tc materials, beyond the cuprates, with Tc raised above 50 K within months. It was a materials discovery verified experimentally and affected the understanding of unconventional superconductivity.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group (Kamihara et al.) made the original report with Tc of 26 K; Chen and Zhao's groups quickly pushed Tc to 43-55 K in Sm and other compounds. The original discovery is clearly Hosono's; the later contributions raised Tc but are second-wave results, which my view of the mandate treats more cautiously. A one-person or Hosono-plus-one prize may be the fairest configuration, but I have to pick from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and rapidly in many laboratories. After more than fifteen years, the pairing mechanism remains debated and no applications have emerged at the level of cuprates, so the lasting impact is more modest.
uncertainties: Whether Chen and Zhao are second-wave contributors rather than original discoverers.
Pairing mechanism remains unresolved, which limits the clarity of the achievement.
Cuprate prize of 1987 may set a high standard for comparable recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube observed a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013 and evidence for a source (TXS 0506+056 in 2017, NGC 1068 in 2022), opening neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. It is an original experiment in an extreme environment with a substantial scientific consequence.
assessment.attribution: IceCube is a collaboration of about 300 scientists; Halzen conceived and led it, while Karle and Spiering held key roles in design, construction and analysis. The collaboration character of the discovery makes the choice of a trio an unusual simplification, and I am uncertain whether these three best capture the decisive contributions, including AMANDA precursors.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by independent analyses, and source identification is progressing but still limited to a few objects. Neutrino astronomy is young and recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Attribution inside a large collaboration is difficult and Nobel rules restrict to three.
Source evidence is at the 3-4 sigma level for individual objects.
Precursor work (DUMAND, Baikal, AMANDA) may need acknowledgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells launched topological insulators as a major field in condensed matter physics, with consequences for spintronics and quantum materials. It is a clear case of theory followed by decisive experiment.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological classification and quantum spin Hall effect in graphene; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe; Molenkamp's group made the 2007 experiment. Credit is shared with Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes, Fu and Moore for 3D topological insulators and with Haldane's earlier work (already recognised in 2016), so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation with many material realisations, though practical impact has been limited so far and the 2016 prize already acknowledged topological phases. Recognition would be timely but must avoid duplication.
uncertainties: Contested credit with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Hasan.
Overlap with the 2016 Nobel Prize for topological phase transitions.
Applications remain prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Titanium-sapphire gain media and semiconductor saturable absorber mode-locking made compact, robust femtosecond lasers possible, and they underlie ultrafast spectroscopy, frequency combs and attosecond science, a field that the 2023 prize recognised. It is an enabling invention with a very broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Moulton invented and demonstrated the Ti:sapphire laser in 1982; Keller invented SESAM mode-locking in the 1990s and made it a practical technology. Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking in Ti:sapphire in 1991, so Sibbett's role is also important, and allocating between SESAM and Kerr-lens routes is unresolved. I choose the two clearest original inventors while noting the third name could be argued. Including a woman inventor is consistent with the committee's stated wish to widen nominations, but the case must stand on the original work.
assessment.maturity: Technology is established and independently confirmed worldwide. Recognition might be seen as late and as overlapping with the 2018 chirped-pulse prize and the 2005 comb prize, which reduces novelty of the claim.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for ultrafast optics and frequency combs.
Allocation among Moulton, Keller and Sibbett is not settled by the supplied record.
Whether this is a discovery or a lifetime-achievement style recognition of technology.
